item.title: The Ripple Effect of Going for It
item.description: Can you learn to captain a yacht at 62 and turn it into a world-traveling lifestyle? Absolutely! Below, Sine Maria shares a first-hand account of her family’s latest charter with Dream Yacht in the Balearic Islands. Read on for an inspiring look at courage, partnership, and what happens when you say yes to a new adventure on the water. The Ripple Effect of Going for It On breaking into worlds you weren’t born into, and what happens when you actually do the thing. By: Good Life Designed and Sine Maria If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my mom, it’s that life has so much to offer and the limit of your world is only limited by your ability to keep expanding. In the middle of the pandemic, as part of our collective pause, she and I decided to go through the whole Good Life Designed program together again. It was through that process that she decided she wanted to be closer to nature, swim more, and learn how to sail. She didn’t grow up around sailing, knew it was costly and a bit of a boys club, but always admired the access it gave those who knew how. That hobby could take you anywhere in the world. The world of sailing requires a unique blend of resources, courage, technical education, practice, and willing crew members to go along for the ride and be there while you figure things out on your first trips alone. It thrives behind heavy yacht club doors that some are born with access into – but most don’t even know exist. The dream of being certified as a sailor has an even smaller niche- attracting those who thrive on the pressure to read and respond to the chaos of the elements at sea while holding the responsibility of passengers’ lives in their hands. Now that I have experienced the reward that comes with that kind of responsibility – I see the draw. Breaking Into a World You Weren’t Born Into I tried to look into data about women certified sailors but couldn’t find any credible data because no one seems to be particularly interested in that stat – however I can tell you there aren’t many. Sailing, just due to the nature of it, the time it requires, the unease that comes with the experience, especially as you’re getting your first solo trips under your belt, is enough to send anyone right over the edge. It’s heady, it’s overwhelming, it’s complicated, it’s technical, and it feels uncertain and dangerous before you’re skilled and experienced enough to feel truly comfortable and at ease on the water. When Pernille got the ping to learn to sail, the biggest question was how, as a 62-year-old woman, was she going to do it. She tried visiting yacht clubs but as someone who wasn’t interested in the social component and was really looking for the technical skills to captain her own ship, it didn’t feel like the best place to spend her time or money. The classes and day sail opportunities to get out on the water were nice, but if she really wanted to learn everything she needed to, she needed something different. She came across Nautilus Sailing, a week-long course in the Sea of Cortez that would teach you everything you need to know about sailing and cap off the week with a test that would certify you to sail on your own anywhere in the world. My dad at the time was in the most stressful period of his career, navigating his independent school and their 400 families through Covid. Using his coveted spring break to learn to navigate another set of uncharted territories felt not quite like the vacation he needed. But he took a leap of his own and joined her anyway. They spent a week disconnected from everything to focus on learning the thing that would later give them access to the life they live now – barely imaginable to them then. Heading out on what feel like once-in-a-lifetime week long sailing experiences all over the world with friends and family. item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. item.title: Mediterranean Sailing: Find the Right Island for You
item.description: Which Is The Best Mediterranean Island For You? Find Out Here! Whether you’re a boating aficionado or new to the art of sailing, there’s no doubt about it – Mediterranean island holidays are among the best in the world. The only downside of sailing the Mediterranean is choosing your destination from our 17 amazing base locations! From relaxing beaches and mouth-watering cuisine to historic marvels and action-packed hiking, anything is possible in the Mediterranean. Ready to experience the region at its best? With a Mediterranean yacht charter, you can easily visit the world’s most sought-after destinations in Greece, Italy, Croatia, Spain, and France – all from the comfort of your liveaboard yacht. If you’re unsure which Mediterranean island holidays you should visit, keep reading to discover the right destination for you. Which Is The Best Mediterranean Island For You? Find Out Below! Split, Croatia: for the Wine Enthusiasts If you’re all about wine tasting, you can’t miss Croatia . And if you’re sailing Mediterranean seas, you can’t miss Split and the Istrian peninsula. Depart from Trogir to sail to Split, Croatia’s second-largest city and a vibrant cosmopolitan hub with an abundance of high-end culinary options. It’s also located on the shores of the Adriatic Sea, giving visitors easy access to some of the Mediterranean’s most beautiful shores. Be sure to save time for a day trip – or an entire stop – in Hvar. This magnificent island attracts global travelers with its white-washed towns, cobblestone streets, clear blue shores, and home-style restaurants with incredible wine. If the wine weren’t enough, everything in this coastal paradise is the definition of picture-perfect. With sweeping natural views this stunning, each glass of wine tastes even better than the last! Greek Islands: Where History Fans Thrive If you have a passion for history, there’s one country you can’t miss: Greece . With Athens, Corfu, and more than 200 idyllic islands, Greece has an endless supply of ancient historic sites to visit. Although Athens isn’t on the coast, it’s easy to visit before or after your Mediterranean yacht charter. This ancient capital is home to the Acropolis and the Parthenon, arguably the most famous sites in Western history. Both are nearly 2,500 years old! If you have time, the Temple of Hephaestus, Mount Lycabettus, the Panathenaic Stadium, and the Ancient Agora of Athens are also essential Athens stops. As for the islands, history buffs will also love Corfu , where the first university and theater in Greece were founded. Santorini and Mykonos also attract history lovers, so don’t forget to add them to your yacht hire Mediterranean itinerary! Sardinia: for Beach Lovers Of the many Mediterranean island vacations to choose from, Sardinia might just have the most impressive beaches . As the second-largest island in the Mediterranean (after Sicily), this Italian paradise has sprawling, sparkling shores you could spend a lifetime exploring. What makes this destination so special? Each of the white sand, crystal clear blue water beaches offers something different. Aruttas and Spiaggia di Piscinas are great for solitude, while Chia is more family-friendly. Spiaggia Rena Bianca offers unmatched swimming, while Cala Goloritzè is perfect for beachfront hiking and climbing. The list is endless! For a more urban experience, sail over to Cagliari, the island’s capital city. It’s the perfect place to alternate between museums, restaurants, and unforgettable beach days. Mljet & Krka National Park: Natural Beauty at Its Best Although Mediterranean island vacations are usually focused on the beach, nature lovers can also explore national parks by yacht. We especially recommend this strategy for Krka National Park and Mljet National Park, two of Croatia’s most stunning natural wonders. item.title: The 15 Best Mediterranean Beaches You Need To Visit
item.description: The Mediterranean is a treasure trove of some of the best beaches in the world. With nearly 30,000 miles of coastline spread across 22 different countries, there’s a reason the Med is one of the most popular tourism destinations on the planet. From vast sandy beaches to secluded bays and pebbled shores, there’s endless choice when it comes to picking the perfect Mediterranean vacation spot. In this post, we round up some of the very best Mediterranean beaches in this European paradise, including a few truly special locations, only accessible by boat. Get ready to experience some serious wanderlust as we take you through the 15 best Mediterranean beaches to visit. What are the Best Beaches in Croatia? Stiniva Beach, Vis This beautifully secluded beach on the island of Vis has previously been voted the best in Europe, and it isn’t hard to see why. Located in the balmy waters of the Adriatic (the northernmost arm of the Mediterranean), Vis is an island paradise of hidden caves and ancient ruins. Stiniva Beach lies on its southern coast and is only accessible by boat or on foot. Like most Croatian beaches, Stiniva’s shoreline is pebbled rather than sandy – but don’t let that put you off. With nothing to cloud the waters, the seas here are crystal clear, and there are some seriously impressive cliffs to dive off if you’re of the thrill-seeking persuasion. Zlatni Rat, Brač One of Croatia’s most recognisable locations, Zlatni Rat is a stunning expanse of fine-pebble beach on the island of Brač. It’s the country’s top windsurfing spot, and with scuba diving and snorkelling available too, Zlatni Rat is one of the best Mediterranean beaches for sports watersports enthusiast. The village of Bol, home to some exceptional restaurants and cafes, is also nearby for a pre or post beach pitstop. Explore the best beaches in Croatia by yacht > What are the Best Beaches in France? Mala Plage, Cap d’Ail Known as one of the most beautiful beaches on the French Riviera, Mala Plage is located in the seaside commune of Cap-d’Ail. It’s a spectacular stretch of white sand and pebbles, surrounded by breathtaking cliffs (not to mention some excellent bars and restaurants). The azure waters are perfect for a leisurely swim, or you can rent a lounger to lay back and soak up the Mediterranean sun. The beach is accessible by boat or on foot from the nearby train station, but bear in mind there’s a long flight of stairs to factor in if you’re planning to walk! Île Sainte Marguerite, Cannes Together with its neighbor Saint-Honorat, Sainte Marguerite makes up one half of the îles de Lérins off the coast of Cannes. It’s easily reached by a short ferry, or you can enjoy its unspoilt beaches from the privacy of your own yacht. The majority of the island is covered in protected forest, and there are countless secluded coves to explore, making it one of the beach Mediterranean beaches for nature lovers. For a day of sunbathing though, there’s one long stretch of sandy beach that’s perfect for families and sun worshippers alike. There are no cars on the island and only a few spots to eat, so don’t expect an all-inclusive resort experience. But when it comes to unspoilt nature and breathtaking views, Île Saint Marguerite is one of the true jewels of the Mediterranean. Explore the best beaches in France by yacht > What are the Best Beaches in Greece? Elafonissi Beach, Crete Made up of literally thousands of islands and islets, Greece is one of the world’s most popular destinations for sailing and yachting excursions. For many people, its sandy shorelines are the epitome of Mediterranean beauty and charm. And while there’s stiff competition, Elafonissi beach on the island of Crete has a serious claim to be one of the very best beaches in the Mediterranean. Its stunning pink sands and turquoise waters mean it could be mistaken for a Caribbean island. With its warm, shallow waters, Elafonissi is great for paddling with young children.
